residue.text: Retained unexplained evidence: 900 rpm side spreads were 11, 3, 12 percent with approximately 12 mm depression; 300 rpm gave 8, 6, 5 percent and approximately 3 mm depression. Transient middle-region specks do not identify bubbles. Matched 900 rpm final vials and bubble measurements are absent; bubble entrainment remains a hypothesis.

Retained measurement limits: common-aliquot readings 0.205, 0.207, 0.206 establish synthetic repeatability, not concentration calibration. Actual rpm is unverified; sampling and transfers may disturb gradients. Record sampling order and raw readings. Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous operation remain untested.

Retained attribution limits: timer-stopped and enabled-rule trials can have unequal quiet durations before second 120. Prompt image changes after stopping may reflect surface shape, settling or other optics; they cannot establish uniformity before cessation or prove a return loop. Persisting images with successful vials could instead support a persistent-artifact hypothesis.

Retained optional proposal, conditional on trial capacity: reverse the fixed-speed pair and insert matched stir-off observations at seconds 45–50, resume, and stop at 65 for 60 total stirring seconds. This hypothesis test is separate from uninterrupted lower-speed repeats. Pauses alter transport; limited replication and order effects constrain conclusions.

summary.text: Observed bounded counterexample: one 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 yielded final vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. Sustained 900 rpm with optical stability is therefore not universally necessary for this sample proxy. Reliable lower-speed sufficiency remains a hypothesis.

Proposed construction: repeat fresh 150 mL water/0.30 mL dye trials at commanded 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, without restart before second-120 sampling. Log five-second side checks without control authority. Fix bottle, camera, addition location and references; alternate depth order. Target final spread at most 4 percent; report readings, durations and failures. Six trials maximum; use spill tray and stop escaping liquid.

Competing hypotheses: reliable fixed lower-speed mixing predicts repeated sample success despite optical failures. Exceptional or sampling-mediated success predicts repeated target failures or sampling-order dependence. Failure challenges reliability without establishing 900 rpm necessity.

Proposed return-link test: compare fixed 60-second 900 rpm with the enabled optical rule capped at second 105; log shadow-rule decisions and final vials at 120. Hypothesis: agitation renews optical disturbance, prolonging stirring. Both succeeding with less timer-controlled stirring supports costly feedback in this comparison; timer failure with enabled success favors useful additional mixing. Neither identifies bubbles.

Proposed reversed-arrow test: compare fixed-duration 300/900 rpm runs and matched post-stop images with equal quiet intervals. Hypothesis: agitation causes transient optical disturbance; falling spread after cessation with successful final vials supports that arrow. Genuine gradients or persistent artifacts remain rivals. Prioritize comparisons within six trials; baseline stirring-time savings remain unknown.
